# {{project.name}}

> HTML-first, framework-independent routing built with native Custom Elements and `@beforesemicolon/web-component`.

Package: `{{project.name}}`
Version: `{{project.version}}`
Documentation: https://router.beforesemicolon.com/documentation/
Complete context: https://router.beforesemicolon.com/llms-full.txt

Use this file as the authoritative compact contract when generating Router code. Do not substitute React Router, JSX routes, hooks, or framework-specific navigation APIs.

## Before Semicolon ecosystem

The packages form one composable browser ecosystem:

1. `@beforesemicolon/markup` provides reactive templates, state, effects, refs, and helpers.
2. `@beforesemicolon/web-component` builds native reactive Custom Elements and re-exports Markup.
3. `@beforesemicolon/router` provides URL routing, navigation, route guards, route modules, route data, and route-aware elements.
4. `@beforesemicolon/intl` provides locale scopes, translations, and internationalized formatting inside any route or component.

Router depends on Web Component internally but exports Router APIs, not the Web Component or Markup APIs. Import `html`, `WebComponent`, or `css` from `@beforesemicolon/web-component` when application code needs them.

Canonical ecosystem contracts:

- https://markup.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt
- https://web-component.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt
- https://intl.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt

## Installation and registration

```bash
npm install @beforesemicolon/router
```

Import the package once to register its Custom Elements:

```javascript
import '@beforesemicolon/router'
```

Import programmatic APIs from the same package:

```javascript
import {
    goToPage,
    replacePage,
    onPage,
    onPageChange,
    updateSearchQuery,
    registerRouteGuard,
    registerGlobalGuard,
    registerRouteModules,
} from '@beforesemicolon/router'
```

For direct browser use, Web Component must load first:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@beforesemicolon/web-component/dist/client.js"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@beforesemicolon/router/dist/client.js"></script>
<script>
    const { goToPage, onPageChange, updateSearchQuery } = BFS.ROUTER
</script>
```

## Route elements

Use Router's HTML elements directly:

```html
<nav>
    <page-link path="/">Home</page-link>
    <page-link path="/projects">Projects</page-link>
</nav>

<page-route path="/">Home page</page-route>
<page-route path="/projects">Projects page</page-route>
<page-route path="*">
    Not found. <page-redirect path="/"></page-redirect>
</page-route>
```

Important elements:

- `<page-route>` renders inline, fetched, or module-based content when its path matches.
- `<page-link>` performs Router navigation using `path` and query updates using `search`.
- `<page-data>` renders route params, query values, or navigation data.
- `<page-route-query>` conditionally renders against a query value.
- `<page-redirect>` redirects an active route.

Use `path`, not React-style `to` or a native `href`, on `<page-link>`.

## Route patterns and nesting

Dynamic parameters begin with `:`:

```html
<page-route path="/users/:userId">
    User: <page-data param="userId">unknown</page-data>
</page-route>
```

Set `exact="false"` on layout routes that should remain active for descendants:

```html
<page-route path="/projects/:projectId" exact="false">
    <aside>
        <page-link path="$/overview">Overview</page-link>
        <page-link path="$/settings">Settings</page-link>
    </aside>

    <page-route path="/overview">Overview</page-route>
    <page-route path="/settings">Settings</page-route>
</page-route>
```

- `$` resolves from the closest ancestor route.
- `~` resolves from the current browser pathname.

## Lazy route modules

`src` may load HTML, text, or a JavaScript module. A JavaScript route module exports a default rendering function:

```javascript
import { html } from '@beforesemicolon/web-component'

export default (data, params, query) => html`
    <h1>Project ${params.projectId}</h1>
    <p>Filter: ${query.filter || 'all'}</p>
    <p>Opened from: ${data.from || 'direct visit'}</p>
`
```

Keep rendering imports in Web Component. Router does not export `html`.

## Programmatic navigation

Navigation functions are asynchronous:

```javascript
await goToPage('/users/42', { from: 'search' }, 'User 42')
await replacePage('/login', { reason: 'expired' }, 'Login')
```

Use:

- `goToPage` to push a history entry.
- `replacePage` to replace the current entry.
- `previousPage` and `nextPage` for history movement.
- `updateSearchQuery` to update serialized query state.
- `getPageData`, `getPageParams`, and `getSearchParams` to read current values.
- `onPage` for a specific route and `onPageChange` for general navigation subscriptions.

```javascript
const unsubscribe = onPageChange((pathname, searchParams, pageData) => {
    console.log(pathname, searchParams, pageData)
})

unsubscribe()
```

## Guards and metadata

Guards return or resolve to:

- `true` to allow navigation.
- `false` to block navigation.
- A path string to redirect.

```javascript
registerGlobalGuard((pathname) => {
    if (pathname.startsWith('/account') && !auth.isSignedIn()) {
        return '/login'
    }

    return true
})
```

Use `registerRouteGuard` for a registered route and `getRouteMeta` for route metadata. Guard registration does not return an unsubscribe function.

## Route modules

Register module loaders centrally by their route source paths when routes should preload or resolve them without an extra dynamic lookup:

```javascript
registerRouteModules({
    './pages/dashboard.js': () => import('./pages/dashboard.js'),
    './pages/settings.js': () => import('./pages/settings.js'),
})
```

Use `getRouteModule`, `resolveRouteModule`, `preloadRouteModule`, and `preloadRouteModules` for explicit control.

## Web Component and Intl composition

Router owns navigation; Web Component owns application components; Intl owns localized output. They work in the same DOM tree:

```bash
npm install @beforesemicolon/router @beforesemicolon/intl
```

```javascript
import '@beforesemicolon/router'
import '@beforesemicolon/intl'
```

```html
<page-route path="/products/:productId">
    <intl-locale locale="en-US" src-dir="/locales">
        <h1><intl-msg key="products.detail">Product</intl-msg></h1>
        <intl-number type="currency" currency="USD">49.99</intl-number>
    </intl-locale>
</page-route>
```

For CDN use, load scripts in this order: Web Component, Router, Intl. Router and Intl may be reversed relative to each other, but both must follow Web Component.

## Rules for generated code

- Use Router Custom Elements and APIs exactly as documented.
- Import `html` and `WebComponent` from `@beforesemicolon/web-component`, never from Router.
- Use `path` and `search` on `<page-link>`; do not generate React Router props or hooks.
- Put durable identifiers in path params, filtering and view state in search params, and transient handoff data in navigation data.
- Await programmatic navigation when subsequent work depends on completion.
- Register the package entrypoint once before relying on its Custom Elements.
- Read the Intl contract before adding localized route content.
